results.title: Put Two Videos Side by Side with FFmpeg: hstack, vstack, xstack
results.content:
The layout string reads as coordinate pairs separated by `|`, where `w0` and `h0` mean "the width of input 0" and "the height of input 0." So `w0_h0` is the bottom-right tile. Output here is 1280x720. Recent FFmpeg builds also accept `grid=2x2` as shorthand, which saves you the coordinate arithmetic. Run `ffmpeg -h filter=xstack` to confirm your build has it before you rely on it in a script.

If you pass a layout with fewer entries than inputs, xstack fails with a complaint about undefined windows rather than guessing. That strictness is why xstack is safe to generate programmatically and painful to type by hand. [...] ## xstack handles 2x2 grids and anything larger

For four clips in a quad view, `xstack` is the filter, and it needs an explicit `layout` describing where each input's top-left corner sits. Every tile still has to be scaled first, and every tile dimension should be even so libx264 can encode yuv420p without complaint. [...] Most guides hand you `hstack=inputs=2` and stop there. That command works on two clips exported from the same camera on the same day, which is why it survives in blog posts, and it falls over on real footage. The filter isn't broken. hstack is a compositing primitive, not a layout engine, and it assumes you already did the normalizing yourself.

## hstack matches on height, vstack matches on width

FFmpeg's hstack filter places inputs left to right and requires all of them to be the same height and the same pixel format. vstack places inputs top to bottom and requires the same width. Miss either and FFmpeg stops at graph configuration time with a message like `Input 1 height 720 does not match input 0 height 1080`, followed by `Failed to configure output pad on Parsed_hstack_0`.

results.title: XStack: A Benchmark for ML Repo Migration
results.content:
What the judges find. Apart from broken freezes,
the judges catch two kinds of false positives. The grader reads whatever
number the run reports, which may not be the recipe’s own, such as a
separate validation pass in place of the recipe’s averaged loss; the
correctness judge finds the recipe’s number in the run’s logs and checks
it, so every pass is a true positive. The cheat judge catches cheating, such as training on another task’s machine or reading
another session’s files. [...] Issue-resolution benchmarks (Jimenez et al., 2024; Zan et al., 2025) start from broken code and ask agents to fix it, while conversion benchmarks (Wang et al., 2026c; Song et al., 2026; Hong et al., 2026) compare translated code with the original on the same machine. In our case, the repository already works on the original machines. The challenge is to preserve that behavior while moving the entire system onto hardware the original code does not support. We introduce XStack (XStack stands for Cross-Stack Benchmark) to test this directly. Each task gives an agent a working PyTorch repository and a clean TPU machine, then asks it to rebuild the code on TPU with JAX and make an original experiment run end to end and reach its published result. [...] if it meets our grading criteria, based on the source repository’s published result, authenticated and calibrated by us. Migration by agents remains unreliable: Claude Opus 5 passes 75%, GPT-5.6-sol 45%, and every other agent at most 40%. XStack is a step toward freeing ML code from its ecosystem. We release XStack to make progress toward reliable migration across frameworks and hardware measurable.

# X is down for thousands of users who complain of broken timelines, error messages on platform

By

Ariel Zilber

Published  June 22, 2026, 10:18 a.m. ET

See more of our coverage in your search results.

X users were left staring at error messages and broken timelines Monday morning after Elon Musk’s social media platform suffered a widespread outage that triggered a flood of complaints across the internet.

Problems appeared to begin shortly after 9 a.m. Eastern time, according to Downdetector, which showed reports of issues with X skyrocketing to nearly 30,000 within minutes after tracking only a handful of complaints earlier in the morning. [...] Users quickly flocked to Downdetector’s comment section, turning the outage page into a makeshift chat room while waiting for service to return.

Screenshot of the X (formerly Twitter) interface showing   3

A photo from an X user showing the social media platform not loading.

 

Graph showing a sharp increase in reports, from a baseline of 15 to 32,932 by 9:58 AM on June 22, 2026.  3

“X isn’t loading,” one user wrote.

Another user reported a more specific glitch, saying the platform appeared partially functional but key features were broken.
